context:
Goal: each rule has one home; no stale copy of it lives on.
Problem (rule): 8 agent files held a 5-word fragment of a rule sentence that had been reworded. After the fix, nothing stops the old fragment from being pasted back.
Based on (read): the plan, part b; lint/test_retired_names.py fails any file that holds a listed phrase as a whole word, except GLOSSARY.md and docs/records.md.
Departs from: main lists no retired rule phrases — the old fragment joins the list.

options.gain: The old wording can never return unnoticed.
options.label: Yes: ban it after the fixes (recommended)
options.lose: A file that quotes it on purpose also fails, unless it is one of the two exempt files.

options.gain: No false alarm on a quote.
options.label: No: leave it unlisted
options.lose: The old copy can creep back with no check to catch it.

reply: You picked a: ban the old phrase after the fixes. Home: step one-home-check. Closed 12:40 CST.
short: One-home Q1 of 5: ban an old rule phrase once fixed?
title: One-home check, question 1 of 5: once the old copies of a moved rule are fixed, should their old wording be banned so it cannot come back?
